excludedWorkloads.reason: Collectible CoreCLR generation replacement and Puerts module-cache reexecution are different mechanisms, so their latency is diagnostic rather than a broad gameplay ratio.

regressionGates.rationale: Keeps the generated scalar ABI within a reviewed 48.8 percent ceiling above the M10.1 16.802 ms median while the stricter dedicated ABI ratio gate remains unchanged.
Borrowed fixed-value snapshots must remain allocation-free in the measured managed loop.
One acquisition plus 16,384 borrowed rows must stay below five milliseconds on the frozen UE 5.8.1 host.
Buffered generated event iteration must remain allocation-free in the measured managed loop.
One acquisition plus 65,536 buffered events must stay below five milliseconds on the frozen UE 5.8.1 host.
Caps the existing M10.1 per-frame Actor path at twice its 0.006 ms reference median.
Caps the existing 1,000-entity path below twice its 0.229 ms M10.1 reference median.
Preserves the existing single-batch trace advantage with a reviewed ceiling above the 0.440 ms M10.1 reference.
Prevents the existing load/spawn/destroy path from regressing more than 29.9 percent above its 9.621 ms M10.1 median.
Preserves the complete Demo median with a reviewed ceiling above the 0.582 ms M10.1 result.
Preserves the complete Demo p95 tail with a reviewed ceiling above the 1.060 ms M10.1 result.
Preserves the complete Demo p99 tail with a reviewed ceiling above the 1.403 ms M10.1 result.
Preserves the complete Demo bridge path with a reviewed ceiling above the 175.497 ms M10.1 result.
Keeps the matched delivery-size overhead within five percent while runtime dependencies are hardened.

revisionNotes: Suite 1.1.0 preserves the frozen 1.0.0 manifest and changes only the two high-volume stable data shapes selected by M10.2 profiling.
Delegate count changes from 100,000 to the generated channel's declared 65,536-entry bound on both runtimes.
Every absolute ceiling is derived from the published M10.1 reference and can move only through a reviewed version-control change.
A neutral or losing weighted result remains publishable; only a ratio at or below 0.95 qualifies the broad performance claim.
